title: Usage Priority Tiers and Soft-Quota Arbitration for Mixed-Billing Customers
creator: Aisha Carter
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers increasingly mix committed credits, per-route free allowances, and burst credits. When they exceed a plan quota we currently apply hard throttles or immediate overage billing which causes instability for latency-sensitive routes (e.g., chat flows) and surprises on invoices.

Goal: Design and specify a soft-quota arbitration layer that: 1) prioritizes requests by configured usage tiers (route, caller, org-level); 2) applies a deterministic soft-degradation policy (soft-throttle, delayed overage tagging, queued burst windows) before triggering hard throttles or billing; and 3) emits clear telemetry and invoice line items so customers and support teams can reconcile behavior.

Scope: Product requirements and acceptance criteria for the entitlement arbitration engine and billing trigger integration. Implementation work will be coordinated with Billing, Runtime, and Console teams. This ticket focuses on requirements, UX, and acceptance tests; engineering tickets created separately for runtime and billing services integration.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable priority tiers: Admins can define up to 5 priority tiers (0-4) at org, project, route, and caller levels; the final effective tier resolves by: caller -> route -> project -> org. Default is tier 2.

Soft-quota window behavior: When effective usage reaches 100% of a quota, requests are placed into a 10s soft-window where low-priority requests are delayed up to 500ms and high-priority requests are forwarded without delay. Both window length and max delay are configurable per-plan.

Burst credits arbitration: If burst credits exist, they are consumed preferentially for requests in tiers 0-1. If burst credits are exhausted, fall back to soft-quota behavior before hard throttle or overage billing.

Telemetry: Console shows per-tenant time-series for 'soft-window starts', 'soft-delays applied', 'burst-credit consumption', and 'overage-eligible events' with sampling at 1s resolution for the last 24h and 1m for 90d.

Billing trigger: Only events tagged as 'overage-eligible' during the final reconciliation window (end of billing period or committed-commitment-exhaustion) result in invoiceable overage lines; transient soft-delays must not generate immediate charges unless configured by a plan override.
Audit logs: All arbitration decisions (resolved tier, burst credit used, delay applied, decision timestamp) are emitted to the audit log stream and accessible via Console for 90 days.

Admin UX: Console UI exposes a 'soft-quota simulator' where admins can run synthetic traffic scenarios to preview which requests would be delayed, which would consume burst credits, and potential invoice exposure for the simulation period.

API contract: Public API returns header hints X-Redwood-Quota-State and X-Redwood-Delay-Applied for each request during soft windows. SDKs to surface these headers in the client response object with a stable schema.
Rollback safety: Default behavior must not increase customer charges compared to current production behavior; feature is opt-in per-tenant until fully validated and launched.

End-to-end tests: Automated tests validate arbitration for combinations: (route-priority, caller-priority, burst-available, quota-exhausted) and assert that billing-service receives overage events only when acceptance criteria 5 is met.

Support playbook: A playbook document is available describing how Support can interpret soft-quota telemetry, how to adjust tiers and burst credits, and steps to issue remedial credits if misconfiguration causes customer-facing regressions.
Compliance: For tenants with Private deployment or SOC-sensitive plans, arbitration decision logs must be optionally exportable to customer-managed S3 for the billing reconciliation window.
